text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
The International Monetary Fund's representative in Poland said economic growth of five to six percent and inflation below 18 percent were possible for the country this year.
The Huta Ferrum foundry plans to allot 90 million zlotys for the purchase and construction of a high-tech production line producing steel pipes.
Strzelec brewer plans a public offering for the first quarter next year.
The International Finance Corporation plans to invest about $100 million in Poland in the fiscal year ending on June 30, 1997.
By the end of the year Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy (BPH) will have a computer system in place connecting all its branches in the country.
Shares in insurer Polisa may be listed on both the bourse and the Polish OTC market, which has yet to begin trade. PARKIET
By the end of October Bank Handlowy is expected to apply to the Russian central bank for an operating licence.
